extracted.intended_audience: congressional staff, defense policymakers, oversight bodies, and government procurement/competitive sourcing officials
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, legal requirements, and practical criteria for conducting and overseeing OMB Circular A-76 public-private (competitive sourcing) studies (illustrated by the Walter Reed A-76 case), including timeframes, required officials, PWS content, certification, notice requirements, and cost-comparison considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for completion of A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: the completion of A-76 studies - 12 months for standard competitions, and 90 days for streamlined competitions. Under this competition, DOD was limited by law to a 30-month time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB reported the average time frame for a standard public-private competition under Circular A-76 completed in FY2006 was just over 13 months; earlier (pre-2003) competitions took two to three years. The report highlights that excessive length increases costs, undermines productivity, and can negate expected savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of competitive sourcing officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Circular also required agencies to appoint competitive sourcing officials, such as the Human Resource Advisor (HRA), Agency Tender Official (ATO), Performance Work Statement (PWS) Team Leader; Source Selection Authority (SSA); Contracting Officer (CO), and Competitive Sourcing Official (CSO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These positions are mandated by the revised Circular to provide defined roles and responsibilities in the A-76 process; duties and actions by these officials (e.g., ATO filing protests) can affect protests/appeals and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) development requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of the PWS is critical to the A-76 process. The PWS describes the work that is to be performed under the competition. It is used to compare the MEO’s cost estimates with the contractor’s cost estimates, and includes all responsibilities and requirements; performance standards, acceptable deviations from the standards, and how the contract will be monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Independent Review Official (IRO) provides an analysis of the PWS for clarity and completeness. Its analysis will provide the baseline for all cost estimates. Accurate, complete PWS development is essential for fair cost comparisons and correct bid evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and certification responsibilities of the Independent Review Official (IRO)/Army Audit Agency (AAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAA served as the Independent Review Official (IRO) to certify the MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRO/AAA must independently review and certify the MEO’s bid proposal; the IRO’s analysis of the PWS provides the baseline for cost estimates. Withdrawal or reversal of certification (as occurred) can materially change competition outcomes and trigger appeals/protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB waiver and limitation on use of prior Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB 'expect(ed) DoD to make final decisions for these cost comparisons (including the WRAMC privatization review) no later than September 30, 2004, the completion date projected by the DoD Competitive Sourcing Official... The DoD Competitive Sourcing Official is responsible for ensuring use of the previous Circular is limited to timely completion or cancellation of any initiative.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DoD wished to continue under the pre-2003 Circular beyond the waiver expiration it needed to request an extension from OMB. Continuing past the waiver deadline without authorization was criticized as improper and contributed to oversight concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and appropriations time limits for multi-function A-76 competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The excessive length of the WRAMC privatization review appears to be in violation of both DoD’s own rules, which limit A-76 privatization reviews for multi-function activities to 48 months, and, more importantly, the Defense Appropriations Bill, which limits A-76 studies for multi-function activities to 30 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense Appropriation bills from FY2000-FY2003 contained 48-month prohibitions; Section 8022 of FY2004 and FY2005 Defense Appropriations reduced the limit to 30 months. Violating these limits can raise Anti-Deficiency Act issues and trigger Congressional scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-Deficiency Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title 31, United States Code (31 U.S.C. § 1341(a)(1)(B)). The Antideficiency Act prohibits government spending in excess of available funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceeding statutory/appropriations time limits or otherwise conducting competitions that cause unauthorized spending may implicate the Anti-Deficiency Act; Congress treats apparent violations seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for reductions-in-force (RIF) tied to A-76 actions
rubrics_metrics.description: 10 U.S.C. 1597(e) states: Involuntary Reductions of Civilian Positions. - The Secretary of Defense may not implement any involuntary reduction or furlough of civilian positions ... until the expiration of the 45-day period beginning on the date on which the Secretary submits to Congress a report ... and a description of any change in workload or positions requirements ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Army had to give Congress at least 45 days' notice of the pending RIF, and give WRAMC employees at least 60 days' notice of a pending RIF. Compliance with these statutory notice periods is required before implementing involuntary personnel actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to account for transition and implementation costs in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition Costs: estimates include VERA/VSIP, severance pay, civilian personnel administration, MEDCOM administration, etc.; the annual savings over the baseline costs will be about $4.5 million. The contractor’s cost proposal for the five-year term was almost $17.5 million less than the government workforce’s cost proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-76 cost comparisons must include transition costs (early retirement/separation incentives, severance, administration) and other implementation costs when calculating net savings; failure to include these can misstate the financial outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of a minimum cost differential to contractor bids
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army’s analysis fails to take into account the $10 million 'minimum cost differential' that federal rules require must be applied to contractor bids to account for costs associated with disruption and loss of productivity related to the competition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal guidance/rules require applying a minimum cost differential to contractor bids to reflect disruption/loss-of-productivity costs; omission of this differential can bias the cost comparison in favor of contracting out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to solicitations that change workload require bid recalculation and careful oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: After many amendments (about 1,500 changes) and revisions to the PWS, significant increases in workload altered the evaluated costs; solicitation amendments were later added, according to GAO, to accommodate the surge in maintenance and upkeep activities needed at WRAMC after the start of combat operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial changes to the solicitation/PWS during a competition require recalculation of bids and can invalidate prior certifications; agencies should limit/amend solicitations transparently and ensure recalculation and re-certification as needed to preserve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness as an evaluative and policy criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for the completion of A-76 privatization reviews are established for a very good reason: such exercises generate significant costs and can undermine productivity. The longer A-76 privatization reviews continue, the higher their costs; and the higher their costs, the less likely that those A-76 privatization reviews will generate any actual savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight bodies and decisionmakers should consider timeliness as a material factor in whether to continue, extend, or cancel a competition because protracted competitions can cause attrition of skilled staff, reduce recruitment, and erode expected savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for regulatory relief for certain facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Panel recommended that the Secretary of Defense provide the secretaries of the military services the opportunity to apply for regulatory relief from future A-76 studies, for WRAMC and other military medical treatment facilities only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a policy recommendation, Congress/DoD can consider granting regulatory relief (i.e., exemption from A-76 studies) for certain categories of installations (e.g., medical treatment facilities) where competition may destabilize mission-critical staffing or operations.
